title: FIRST AMENDMENTS TO AGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND BIRDI SYSTEMS, INC., BURNS ENGINEERING, INC., INFOJINI INC., SATWIC INC., AND SIERRA CYBER, LLC, FOR ON-CALL/AS-NEE
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - FIRST AMENDMENTS TO AGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND BIRDI SYSTEMS, INC., BURNS ENGINEERING, INC., INFOJINI INC., SATWIC INC., AND SIERRA CYBER, LLC, FOR ON-CALL/AS-NEEDED INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
Summary
: Staff requests approval of the First Amendments (Amendments) to Agreement Nos. 24-10046 with Birdi Systems, Inc. (Birdi), 24-10047 with Burns Engineering, Inc. (Burns), 24-10048 with Infojini Inc. (Infojini), 24-10049 with Satwic Inc. (Satwic), and 24-10050 with Sierra Cyber, LLC (Sierra Cyber) (Agreements). Due to the various projects supported, these Agreements align with more than one Strategic Plan Objective. The objectives are Objective 2: An Efficient, Secure, and Sustainable Supply Chain, and Objective 3: Improved Financial Performance of Port Assets. The scope of the Agreements is for information technology services on an on-call, as-needed basis. The term of the Agreements is for three years commencing on September 18, 2024, and expiring on September 17, 2027. The current not-to-exceed amount for all Agreements is a collective pool of $6,000,000. The proposed amendments will increase the collective not-to-exceed amount pool by $3,000,000 to $9,000,000. This increase is necessary due to consolidation of technology consulting contracts, the additional technical resources needed for capital and operating projects, and other essential IT support services. Payment of expenditures incurred under the Agreements will continue to be the financial responsibility of the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department).
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) find that in accordance with the Los Angeles City Charter Section 1022, the services required can be performed more feasibly by outside contractors than by City employees; 3) approve the proposed First Amendments to the Agreements with Birdi Systems, Inc., Burns Engineering, Inc., Infojini Inc., Satwic Inc., and Sierra Cyber, LLC, increasing the collective not-to-exceed amounts from $6,000,000 to $9,000,000; 4) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to said Amendments for and on behalf of the Board; and 5) adopt Resolution No. _____________
